Chapter 1: Living the Dream and Missing the Signs.
There’s a certain comfort that comes with having more than enough, isn’t there? Maybe for you, it’s that feeling when you walk into your home and everything sparkles with newness—or the sheer ease of swiping your card, not even thinking twice.
At first, life really does feel like a chain of small wins. Each promotion, every new gadget or car, even those nods of approval from friends and family—they all make the world seem like it’s rewarding your hard work with something you can actually see and touch. A bigger house, a quicker car, that dream vacation—it all feels like proof you’re on the right track.
Back then, every day carried this sense of momentum. There was always something new to chase, another goal on the horizon. And let’s be honest, everyone around—from coworkers to neighbors, even those distant relatives—seemed to measure what you’re worth by what you could show off or spend. It was easy to get caught up in the rhythm. There’s a kind of pride in being able to provide, in saying yes to every opportunity, in never needing to check the price tag.
But under all that shine, sometimes a quiet unease slipped in. Maybe you felt it in those late-night peeks at your bank statement, or noticed how conversations about money always circled back to what’s next—what’s bigger, what’s better. There were moments when the laughter at a dinner party felt a bit forced, or when the thrill of a new purchase faded way faster than you expected. Still, it was easy to push those feelings aside—because isn’t this what success is supposed to look like?
Most of us don’t even notice the subtle ways that comfort can turn into a trap. Those routines that once felt exciting? They slowly become automatic. That sense of security, built on a steady paycheck and a rising bank balance, starts to feel like something you’ll always have.
It’s only when you look back that the warning signs seem obvious: being a little too confident about your investments, shrugging off debt, just assuming that tomorrow will look exactly like today.
I remember one night, a friend brought up how unpredictable the market was, but before long, the conversation drifted right back to vacation plans. The idea that fortunes could change overnight? It felt distant—almost like it couldn’t possibly happen to us. The unspoken belief was that as long as you worked hard and meant well, nothing truly bad would ever come your way.
But looking back now, it’s clear how the chase for more can blind us to risks quietly building in the background. The comfort of routine, the validation from others, the steady climb up the ladder—it all mixes together to create this illusion of invincibility.
But life? It has a way of reminding us that nothing is ever truly guaranteed. Sometimes, the things we rely on most can vanish in a heartbeat.
